title: Spectral theme fallbacks and density-aware component token mapping
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: create a deterministic token fallback map and component override guidelines that ensure visual fidelity and accessibility across brand themes, high-contrast dark variants, and density modes (compact/comfortable). Scope covers: button states (primary/secondary/ghost), table rows and dividers, chart strokes and fills, toast/surface elevations, icon interaction states, and micro-interaction motion tokens. Deliver a mapping table, Figma component updates, a minimal migration plan for the runtime team, and QA recipes for both automated and visual checks. Constraints: must work with existing token pipeline, support per-customer brand overrides, and keep runtime changes minimal (prefer mapping at the design/system layer).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A token fallback mapping document exists that lists source tokens, fallbacks (with WCAG contrast annotations), and priority order for light/dark/alt brand modes. 2) Figma components for buttons, tables, charts updated with annotation layers showing token fallbacks and density variants. 3) Console component spec doc with behavior for overridden brand colors and a recommended algorithm for selecting accessible accents. 4) Two engineering-facing migration notes: a minimal JSON map and an example of runtime application (prefix/KV cache-safe). 5) QA checklist with 8 scenarios (brand default, alt brand dark, alt brand light, compact density, compact+dark, high-contrast mode, chart palette regressions, button focus rings).
design_decisions: - Prefer composable token layers (base semantic tokens + brand overlay + density modifier) rather than duplicating full palettes per brand. - Use a prioritized fallback list to avoid on-the-fly color generation in the runtime. - For chart accents, pick a primary accessible accent and 3 derived tones with contrast-tested ratios instead of relying on brand-supplied palettes. - Button ghost/outline states should derive ink color from surface/brand tokens with an enforced minimum contrast of 3:1 for interactive affordances. - Avoid changing shadow/elevation tokens; prefer subtle blend overlays to imply elevation on dark surfaces.
risks_and_tradeoffs: - Tradeoff: additional design token complexity vs fewer runtime changes. We accept more design-time config to keep runtime stable. - Risk: some customer brand combos may still fail contrast thresholds; mitigation: document allowed brand ranges and provide a fallback accent selector that can be toggled by platform. - Risk: charts with many series may still need per-customer palette tuning; mitigation: provide a recommended default accessible palette and a pattern for overriding specific series colors.
implementation_notes: - Deliverables: mapping JSON (engineer-friendly), Figma kit updates, confluence doc with examples, and test plan. - File naming convention for tokens: semantic.<token>.<mode> (e.g., semantic.surface.bg.dark). - Density modifier tokens: density.compact.* and density.comfort.* applied as last layer. - Provide a small utility function example for picking fallbacks (pseudocode in confluence). - Coordinate with ENG-40211 for runtime acceptance of the JSON map and ENG-40278 for canary rollout gating.

qa_checklist: Brand default light: compare pixels against baseline, confirm WCAG AA for text >= 14px.
Brand alt dark: verify surface contrast, button states, and focus rings across themes.
Compact density + dark: ensure table dividers and inputs maintain 3:1 contrast for labels.
Comfort density + light: validate chart stroke weights and legend legibility.
High-contrast accessibility mode: ensure forced overrides still render actionable elements visible.
Chart palette regression: run automated palette generator and compare series color contrast matrix.
API-driven brand override: test enterprise-supplied hex values and ensure fallback selection occurs when thresholds fail.
Visual regression: capture screenshots across 5 viewports and run diffing job in theme-visual-regressions dashboard.
